dedupe_keys.name: universal techno economic model utem for access network technologies

description: This doctoral dissertation reviews techno-economic modelling of access network technologies, sets out the characteristics a universal techno-economic model should have, classifies the models found in the literature against them, and then defines and develops the Universal Techno-Economic Model (UTEM) with a methodology to industrialise techno-economic assessment in multiple domains. The model considers the perspectives of all market players and is suitable for technological consulting. Producer: Carlos Bendicho, whose PhD in Telecommunications Engineering was delivered in December 2015 and defended in February 2016; the English translation on arXiv (188 pages, 30 figures, 56 tables) excludes confidential chapters 3 and 4, and the Spanish original is held at the University of the Basque Country repository. Coverage: generic, applicable to any access technology and market. Access: the dissertation is a free PDF on arXiv; the abstract says the UTEM itself is available to industry stakeholders under a specific licence of use, so the software or spreadsheet is not open. Licence and cost: specific licence, cost on request. Caveats: two chapters are confidential, the model implementation is not published, and the thesis dates from 2015. Simulation uses: business-case modelling and comparison of access network technologies for capacity planning and investment decisions. Related record: the India 5G universal broadband techno-economic model (model-india5g-universal-broadband-techno-economic).
